prompt: A satellite moves to an orbit whose radius, measured from the centre of the Earth, is twice its original radius. By what factor does the gravitational field strength at the satellite change?

A satellite orbits Earth at a height of 400 km. (Earth radius $6.37\times10^6$ m, mass $5.97\times10^{24}$ kg, $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N m² kg⁻²)

**(a)** Calculate its orbital speed. **[2]**

**(b)** Calculate its orbital period in minutes. **[2]**

**(c)** Explain why astronauts in the satellite appear weightless. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $r = 6.77\times10^6$ m ✓; $v = \sqrt{GM/r} = 7.67\times10^3$ m s⁻¹ ✓

**(b)** $T = 2\pi r/v = 5.55\times10^3$ s ✓ $\approx 92$ min ✓

**(c)** Astronauts and satellite are in free fall with the same acceleration ✓, so there is no normal (contact) force between them ✓
